fix.summary: Cosmic-ray protons above ~5×10¹⁹ eV photoproduce pions on CMB photons. The threshold follows from the invariant s. These losses limit proton horizons to ~100 Mpc and contribute to the observed flux suppression, alongside possible source-energy limits.

fix.summary: The universe was a quark-gluon plasma until ~10 microseconds, then cooled through the QCD crossover at T_c ~ 156 MeV. Heavy-ion collisions recreate that matter and test the lattice equation of state, which fixes the early-universe expansion rate through that epoch.

fix.summary: BBN abundances measure the radiation-dominated expansion rate H(T) and g_*, testing the Friedmann equation and the relativistic-species content 1-1000 s after the Big Bang, one of the earliest probes of the expansion history.

reason: Stellar depletion is not settled as favoured; the problem remains open between nuclear, stellar and new-physics explanations.

fix.summary: Standard BBN predicts 7Li/H about three times the Spite plateau in metal-poor halo stars; whether the gap is nuclear (7Be destruction rates), stellar (atomic diffusion and mixing in stellar atmospheres) or new physics is unresolved.

reason: The same dark-matter–nucleon scattering physics drives capture, so this is a mechanism link, not an analogy. Still speculative.
'Most of the iron' overstates Type Ia's share of solar Fe, which is roughly half to two thirds.

fix.summary: Core-collapse supernovae make the alpha elements and iron-peak nuclei through explosive burning and the nu-p and weak r-process; thermonuclear (Ia) supernovae make a large share of the iron. Ordinary core-collapse ejecta fail to reach the third r-process peak.
